newsitem.title: BERMUDA: LaSalle Re Q1 net premiums written.
newsitem.headline: LaSalle Re Q1 net premiums written.

text.p: LaSalle Re Holdings Ltd said a decline in first quarter net premiums written to $5.2 million from $12.6 million a year ago was expected and due to several factors.
LaSalle Re said net premiums written declined due to 1996 premium adjustments on quota share contracts of $3.0 million that were not repeated in this quarter.

Lower loss activity led to a reduction in reinstatement premiums of $0.9 million. In addition, there was a change in the renewal date of a significant contract to January 1 from December 1, the company said.
LaSalle Re chief executive Victor H. Blake said the results are a reflection of what is a normally quiet underwriting quarter.
"This quarter is not a significant one in terms of premiums written," he said. "Most of our business renews at other times in the year."
Blake said the company is continuing to generate strong profits, and is meeting its long-term goal of achieving a high annualized return on equity, targeted at between 20-25 percent.
"Competition continued in our sector," he said.

"In the face of this, we are operating profitably by continuing to focus on retaining our core clients, maintaining the broad geographic spread of our risks and diversifying the lines of business we write," he said.
The company said it completed a secondary offering of shares during the quarter in which certain of its founding shareholders reduced their holdings in the company.
Upon completion of the secondary offering, the minority interest in LaSalle Re Limited was reduced to 27 percent from 37 percent.
Founding industry sponsors Aon Corp and CNA Financial Corp maintained their initial positions in the company, LaSalle Re said.

In conjunction with its previously announced enhanced capital management strategy, under which the company intends to pay out 50 percent to 60 percent of prior year's earnings by way of dividends, the company paid a quarterly dividend of 71 cents per share on Jan. 16 to shareholders of record Jan. 2.
This dividend represents 50 percent of fiscal 1996 earnings.
